quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Your mirrors show you everything around your motorcycle.
Check your mirrors and turn your head to look for blind spots.
Use your turn signal and move right or left immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and turn your head to look for blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, even after using your mirrors.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes so they work together when you use the rear brake.
It automatically brakes based on your riding style.
It applies brakes when you shift down to a lower gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes so they work together when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems. When you apply the rear brake, the front and rear brakes work together. Check your owner's manual to learn how your specific motorcycle's brakes work.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Signal ahead
Crossroad ahead
Divided roadway ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that the road ahead is divided.

questions.question: A motorcycle horn is ________ a car horn.

options.text: Louder than
Quieter than
About as loud as

questions.correctAnswerText: Quieter than
questions.explanation: Motorcycle horns are not as loud as car horns. You can use your horn when needed, but do not rely on it to keep you safe.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, a motorcycle rider has an advantage because:

options.text: A motorcycle can speed up faster than a car.
A motorcycle can ride on the left side of the lane to avoid car doors and people.
A motorcycle stops faster than a car.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle can ride on the left side of the lane to avoid car doors and people.
questions.explanation: You can ride on the left side of your lane when passing parked cars on the right. This helps you avoid opening doors, people getting out, or people stepping between cars. Only do this if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Yield to other drivers.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming up.

questions.question: How are convex mirrors different from regular mirrors?

options.text: They show a narrower view of the road.
They show a wider view of the road.
They show a clearer view of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They show a wider view of the road.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are common on motorcycles. They show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, vehicles in convex mirrors may appear farther away than they really are.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right lane ends
Left lane ends
Traffic control device ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that the right lane is ending ahead.

questions.question: In normal conditions, what is the minimum following distance for a motorcycle?

options.text: Two seconds
Three seconds
Four seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds
questions.explanation: Keep at least a two-second distance behind other vehicles in normal conditions. When conditions are not ideal, increase this distance.

questions.question: What is one of the best ways to help others see your motorcycle?

options.text: Flash your lights on and off.
Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: Use your high beam headlight day and night whenever it is legal and safe. This, along with your running lights, helps others see your motorcycle.

questions.question: A DOT-compliant helmet:

options.text: Blocks most of your vision.
Lets you see everything you need to see for safe riding.
Can be dangerous for the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you see everything you need to see for safe riding.
questions.explanation: Many people think helmets limit vision, but this is not true. Any helmet approved by the U.S. Department of Transportation will let you see all that you need for safe riding.

questions.question: At night, you can tell if there are bumps ahead by riding behind another vehicle and:

options.text: Listening for the other vehicle scraping the road.
Watching the other vehicle's taillights bounce up and down.
Looking at the rear bumper to see if it bounces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watching the other vehicle's taillights bounce up and down.
questions.explanation: At night, watch the vehicle ahead of you to check road conditions. If its taillights bounce up and down, there are bumps in the road ahead.

questions.question: Alcohol reaches the brain ________ being consumed.

options.text: within minutes of
about an hour after
about two hours after

questions.correctAnswerText: within minutes of
questions.explanation: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts to affect your riding ability. Riding while under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, the best place to ride is:

options.text: On the right side of the lane.
On the edge of the road.
In the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Rain mixes with oil on the road, making it very slippery. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you because these areas are drier and safer.

questions.question: Riding alongside a vehicle in the next lane is:

options.text: Not recommended because you may be in the driver's blind spot.
Good if you want to travel at the same speed as the other driver.
Okay if you want to race the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not recommended because you may be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. The driver may not see you in their blind spot, and the vehicle will block any escape routes if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Which factor affects a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
The drinker's height
The temperature outside

questions.correctAnswerText: The amount of alcohol consumed
questions.explanation: The main factors that affect BAC are how much alcohol is consumed, how fast it is consumed, and the drinker's body weight.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, your feet should be:

options.text: On the footrests for balance.
Pointed down with toes aiming downward.
Relaxed.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the footrests for balance.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet on the footrests for balance. Do not point your toes downward because they may get caught between the road and the footrests.

questions.question: If you are passing parked vehicles on your right and there is no oncoming traffic, ride:

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane. This helps you avoid opening car doors and pedestrians stepping out from between vehicles. If there is oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane for more space around you.

questions.question: You should not ride directly next to another vehicle because:

options.text: Another driver may want to use your lane to pass.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You may have access to escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. You may be in the driver's blind spot, and they will not know you are there. The vehicle will also block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are separated by:

options.text: White lines.
Yellow lines.
Road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed white lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet
Lanes shift
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols or words. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road ahead may be slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the tire locked. It will help you stop faster.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away, then apply it again with gentle pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again with gentle pressure.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the brake pressure immediately. Then slowly apply the brake again with controlled, gentle pressure.

questions.question: What should passengers do?

options.text: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.
Never hold onto the rider.
Do not lean into any turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.
questions.explanation: Before you start riding, tell your passenger to hold firmly onto your hips, waist, or belt. If your motorcycle has secure handholds, your passenger can use those instead.

questions.question: Where is the greatest risk of a crash with other vehicles?

options.text: At an intersection
On the highway
On any road

questions.correctAnswerText: At an intersection
questions.explanation: Intersections are where motorcycles face the greatest risk of crashes with other vehicles.

questions.question: What blood alcohol content (BAC) makes it illegal to ride a motorcycle?

options.text: 0.08 percent or higher
0.1 percent or higher
0.3 percent or higher

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent or higher
questions.explanation: In California, adults age 21 or older cannot ride a motorcycle with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. People under 21 cannot ride with a BAC of 0.01 percent or higher. Riding may be unsafe even below the legal limit.
